content.title: About
content.content: Arepa Dominicana is a traditional corn bread made from pre‑soaked and ground cornmeal (masarepa). The dough is shaped into small round patties and fried on a dry skillet until a golden crust forms. Inside, the arepa is soft and slightly crumbly, while the outside is crisp. It can be enjoyed plain or used as a base for fillings such as meat, cheese, beans, vegetables, or seafood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Although the arepa originates from Venezuela, the Dominican version has its own distinctive flavor thanks to local corn varieties.
Traditionally the dough is left to ferment for several hours, giving it a subtle tangy aroma.
In the Dominican Republic arepas are often served with “moho,” a sauce made from tomatoes, onion, garlic, and hot pepper.
Arepas can be cooked over an open flame or baked in the oven; the latter yields a lighter, airier texture.
Unlike Mexican tortillas, Dominican arepas contain no wheat flour and are completely gluten‑free.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cornmeal provides a slow‑release source of energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Arepas are virtually fat‑free, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for metabolism.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: Mycotoxin risk
items.content: Improperly stored cornmeal can develop mycotoxins; always use fresh, quality ingredients.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Consuming large amounts may cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the arepa hot, split it open and add fillings such as grilled meat, cheese, avocado, beans, salad, or seafood. It can also be used as a sandwich base or paired with moho sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked arepas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Before reheating, let them reach room temperature to avoid dryness.
